page.name: Product UI Basics
page.purpose_summary: Defines the role, scope, and constraints of Product User Interfaces in Bosch products and explains how Product UI guidance extends the Bosch Digital Design System and Bosch Brand Guide for digital interfaces embedded in hardware products.

product_ui.definition: The digital part of a product or device that a person interacts with, mostly through visual and tactile means, to control the product or device as desired.
examples: Kitchen appliance controlled digitally via display
product_ui.required_characteristic: A product with Product UI has at least one digital touchpoint, such as a display or graphical user interface (GUI).
product_ui.multiple_outputs_example: A washing machine may have a display and an additional projected display on the floor.

human_machine_interface.definition: A term more commonly used in the context of machines and devices, often including physical input methods such as buttons, knobs, levers, or steering mechanisms.
human_machine_interface.example: A steering wheel used to control a car.

relationship_between_pui_and_hmi.distinction: Historically distinct, but modern digital products blur the boundaries between Product UI and HMI.
relationship_between_pui_and_hmi.current_usage: The terms are often used synonymously in contemporary language.

no_ui_trend.description: AI and Natural UI can reduce the visual and tactile aspects of user interfaces.

scope.focus: Digital interfaces incorporated into physical Bosch products.
applies_to: Graphical user interfaces embedded in physical products
does_not_focus_on: Machines in the broader HMI sense
Mechanically operated devices without Product UI

relationship_to_other_guidelines.relationship: Product UI Basics extends the Bosch UI Kit for user interfaces integrated into hardware products.
BDDS global rules continue to apply; this page adds Product UI specific principles and exceptions.
Global Bosch brand guidelines continue to apply to Product UIs.
The software styleguide defines digital elements of digital software products, while this Product UI guidance focuses on digital interfaces built into physical products.
Continues to apply to physical product design, especially where hardware input/output is relevant.

design_intent.primary_goal: Create a consistent Bosch experience across multiple products, business units, product groups, and product touchpoints.
design_intent.development_implication: Brand-compliant design must be considered early in Product UI development.
design_intent.experience_context: Digital interfaces are becoming a core component of the overall product experience as boundaries between physical products and their interfaces become more fluid.
design_intent.collaboration_principle: UI designers and product designers should work closely together to integrate display and hardware seamlessly, connecting the physical and virtual parts of the product experience.

technical_limitations.principle: The defined principles should be implemented as well as possible, but technical challenges may require adapted or alternative solutions.

challenges.description: Product UIs may range from simple low-resolution displays to powerful high-resolution displays.
challenges.impact: The same visual principle may need different implementations depending on display capability.

challenges.description: Some displays cannot reproduce full color information.
challenges.impact: Color-dependent communication may require alternative visual encodings.

challenges.description: Graphics processors can have very different performance levels.
challenges.impact: Motion, rendering complexity, or visual richness may need to be adapted to hardware constraints.

resolution_path: Use alternative solutions referenced by the guideline where needed.
Discuss additional alternative solutions with the C/CGB-CD team.

hardware_considerations.focus_statement: The guideline focuses on digital interfaces, but hardware-relevant input and output aspects must still be considered in product design.
hardware_considerations.design_dependency: Hardware interaction can influence Product UI behavior and therefore must be considered together with digital interface design.

content_structure.heading: Product UI Basics
key_points: Focuses on digital interfaces of products.
Extends BDDS rules with Product UI specific principles for layout, grid, colors, and icons.
Addresses digital interfaces incorporated into physical products.

content_structure.heading: The purpose of this guideline
key_points: Provides key design principles for consistent Bosch experiences.
Applies across business units, product groups, products, and touchpoints.
Requires early consideration of brand-compliant design.
Mostly describes exceptions and additions for product-specific user interfaces.

content_structure.heading: Product User Interface (PUI) vs. Human Machine Interface (HMI)

key_points: PUI and HMI definitions come from prior technological developments and do not fully reflect modern interface convergence.
A Product UI is primarily digital, visual, and tactile.
HMI often includes physical input methods and is used more often for machines and devices.
Focuses on Bosch products, not machines or mechanically operated devices in a broader sense.
Product UIs have at least one digital touchpoint.
Digital and physical product design should be integrated.

content_structure.heading: Technical limitations
key_points: Technical diversity can make guideline implementation challenging.
Alternative solutions may be needed for low-resolution displays, monochrome displays, or limited graphics performance.
Hardware input and output aspects remain relevant even when the focus is digital.

callouts.message: This content is an extension of the Bosch UI Kit for the design of user interfaces integrated into hardware products (Product UI).

recommended_use: Use as contextual rules when generating or evaluating Bosch Product UI concepts.
Check whether an interface is embedded in a physical product before applying Product UI guidance.
Treat this guidance as an extension of BDDS and Bosch Brand Guide, not as a replacement.
Account for hardware limitations before enforcing high-fidelity visual rules.

decision_rules.if: The digital interface is integrated into a hardware product
decision_rules.then: Apply Product UI guidance together with Bosch Brand Guide and BDDS rules.

decision_rules.if: The interface belongs to a pure software product
decision_rules.then: Use the software styleguide instead of Product UI specific rules.

decision_rules.if: Display resolution, color, or processing capability is limited
decision_rules.then: Use guideline-supported alternatives or consult the C/CGB-CD team.

decision_rules.if: Physical input/output elements affect user interaction
decision_rules.then: Coordinate Product UI design with Product Design guidance.
